title: Introduce degradation fencing and graceful throttle orchestrator for Dedicated fleets
author: Maya Santoro
release_notes: Adds a degradation fencing layer to Dedicated autoscaler; enables graceful throttling fallback to avoid cascading evictions; gated by feature flag; telemetry and dashboards added.
commits: a1c9f3d: orchestrator: introduce DegradationFence state machine and reconciliation loop
4b2e7a0: autoscaler: graceful throttle policy and soft-failover path
8f7d1c2: telemetry: add degradation_fence.{enter,exit,throttle} metrics and export tags
d3b4f66: tests: unit + integration for fence transitions and edge cases
e6a9a21: docs: add runbook and rollout notes for degradation fencing
body: Context: We observed two production incidents where sudden inter-cluster pressure triggered aggressive eviction paths in Dedicated pools, causing intermittent SLA spikes for latency-sensitive tenants. The root cause was an autoscaler feedback loop that did not distinguish between sustained demand and transient overloads caused by imbalance during node churn. Motivation: Introduce a thin coordination layer — DegradationFence — that tracks per-fleet transient overload signals and gates hard eviction paths behind a graceful throttle/fallback that preserves minimal throughput guarantees for high-priority tenants. Summary of changes: 1) DegradationFence state machine (services/autoscaler/state/fence_state.go) that records ephemeral overload windows, maintains a moving-window score, and exposes decisions via a compact API to the autoscaler. 2) GracefulThrottle policy (policies/graceful_throttle.go) that, when the fence is active, applies tokenized soft-throttles and prefers request shedding and routing fallbacks over pod/GPU evictions. 3) Orchestrator (controller/fence_orchestrator.go) that reconciles fence state across control-plane replicas, persists recent events to the cluster status store for recovery, and emits structured telemetry. 4) Telemetry hooks (metrics_registry.go) with new metrics degradation_fence.enter, degradation_fence.exit, degradation_fence.throttle_count and labels for fleet_id, priority_tier, and window_percentile. 5) Feature flag gating (deploy/feature_flags.yaml) to enable rollout by region and fleet. 6) Runbook and docs (docs/runbooks/dedicated-degradation-fence.md) plus integration tests and chart tweaks. Commits: a1c9f3d | 4b2e7a0 | 8f7d1c2 | d3b4f66 | e6a9a21 CI: full unit suite + autoscaler integration harness ran; a flaky k8s scheduling test was observed and re-run — all checks passed on the final green. Files of note: fence_state.go implements a compact state util with a leaky-bucket timer, policy thresholds are configurable via chart values and feature flags, graceful_throttle contains fallbacks to model-variant routing and token-based request shedding. Testing: Unit coverage added for state transitions and error paths, integration test simulates node churn and verifies no >2x spike in tenant P90 latency under gateway fallbacks. Performance: In the simulation harness with a 2% transient overload injection, the orchestrator prevented any evictions in 87% of runs and reduced median eviction-induced downtime by 63%. Rollout plan: stage behind feature flag in eu-west-1 dedicated fleets at 30% traffic for 48h -> increase to 70% if no regression -> global rollout. Observability: new Grafana dashboard (linked in runbook) surfaces fence activation timelines and throttle counts by tenant; we added an alert SLO_ARMOR_DEGRADATION to page on sustained (>10m) fence activations affecting >5% of capacity. Backwards compatibility: No API surface changes for tenants. All changes are opt-in via feature flag and controlled via chart values. Risk and mitigations: risk of underreacting to genuine capacity pressure leading to sustained latency; mitigated by conservative default thresholds, an emergency override to force hard eviction, and canary rollout. Review summary: initial design review requested additional metrics granularity and a higher-resolution window for priority_tier==platinum; addressed by adding percentile tags and exposing window granularity as a config. Final review approvals: Priya Nair (design + SRE), Ethan Cole (runtime), Luca Romano (infra + release). Merge: squash and merge. Related: ENG-1921 (design epic), SRE-440 (incident follow-up), SUP-989 (support ticket that motivated the runbook).
